observed_behavior: On base SHA 71e7d0289ff04ebb45eb0f09e7e14052cb9f4cd1 with the same 50,000-file, 5,000-page fixture and matching functional digest, BDD-016 has failed when one index_candidate sample took 3.470925499976147 seconds, while retained and controlled repetitions passed.
expected_behavior: The large-repository performance gate must provide a repeatable and explainable verdict for a fixed workload: representative or sustained violations of the 2.0-second contract fail, while an unclassified single timing anomaly does not randomly switch an otherwise identical delivery baseline between pass and fail.
impact: Unrelated deliveries can be blocked by an intermittent owner baseline and then pass on retry, preventing implementers from reliably distinguishing a real performance regression, measurement variance, and an environment failure.

reproduction.symptom_oracle: Repeated runs at the same source SHA, 50k/5k fixture shape, and functional digest alternate between pass and fail without a classified product or environment difference.
steps: From repository root, run python -X utf8 -B .agents/skills/project-knowledge/scripts/test_behavior.py --group delivery --fixture-root .knowledge-test-tmp.
Compare report outcome, functional_sha256, file_count, page_count, and durations_seconds.index_candidate across runs.
Confirm fixture cleanup and a strict-clean repository after each sample.
reproduction.sample: One retained failure had index_candidate=3.470925499976147s with matching functional digest; one retained focused sample passed; five controlled same-SHA samples passed with index_candidate from 0.7987834999803454s to 0.9807830000063404s.

root_cause.summary: The intermittent gate failure is caused at the verdict boundary by mapping one wall-clock index_candidate sample directly to the whole baseline outcome; the underlying source of the latency outlier remains unconfirmed between traversal state, fixture sequence, and external Windows load.

hypotheses.statement: A single wall-clock index_candidate sample determines the complete verdict, so ordinary filesystem or scheduler latency variance is misclassified as a stable performance regression.
hypotheses.variable: Repeat count for the same operation while source, fixture, and functional digest stay fixed.
hypotheses.prediction: The verdict changes with one outlier while adjacent samples remain under the threshold and retain identical functional output.
hypotheses.falsifier: The over-threshold duration is stably reproducible in a fixed environment and traces to the same internal product path rather than sample variance.

hypotheses.statement: A specific predecessor-scenario or fresh-fixture cache state makes the 5,000-page current-page traversal intermittently slow.
hypotheses.variable: BDD predecessor sequence or fresh-versus-reused fixture state.
hypotheses.prediction: Over-threshold samples cluster reproducibly under one sequence or fixture state.
hypotheses.falsifier: Repeated samples show no correlation with sequence or fixture state, or fail at the same rate without predecessors.

hypotheses.statement: External Windows CPU, filesystem-filter, or process pressure is the primary source of the observed latency outlier.
hypotheses.variable: Measured host resource pressure with all repository inputs fixed.
hypotheses.prediction: Outlier frequency rises with external pressure and returns to baseline after the pressure is removed.
hypotheses.falsifier: An isolated low-load run can deterministically toggle the failure through an internal product variable.

next_action: Open an independent BUG delivery requirements stage for a repeatable performance oracle that preserves the 50k/5k fixture, functional digest, and 2.0-second regression contract; do not include the separately unconfirmed Windows Git launch event.
